newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stadshypotek bid process underway - paper.
newsitem.headline: Stadshypotek bid process underway - paper.

text.p: Investment bankers Merrill Lynch are advising the Swedish government on the disposal of its 34 percent shareholding in mortgage bank Stadshypotek, the financial daily Dagens Industri reported on Wednesday.
Swedish banks S-E-Banken, Handelsbanken and Nordbanken are interested and General Electric Capital Corp may also be interested, the paper wrote.

Another paper, Dagens Nyheter, said the reason why Finance Minister Erik Asbrink opposed the planned merger between Stadshypotek and insurer Skandia was because he wanted the mortgage lender to link with Nordbanken.
The paper quoted ministry official Hans Jacobson as denying this.

Dagens Industri said the ministry wanted to shortlist at least two serious bidders and start serious negotiations in the next three weeks. One condition was that the bidder would be obliged to make an offer for the whole of Stadshypotek, it said.
Jacobson could not immediately be reached for comment on the newspaper reports.
Standard & Poor's, affirming on Wednesday the ratings of both Skandia and Stadshypotek, said it believed the companies to be a good match financially.
